files.tomato/__main__.py:
"""The `tomato` command line (D28a, D30a, P35):
  tomato run FILE [ENTRY [INPUTS...]] [--llvm FILE.ll ...]   run a program with the interpreter
  tomato compile FILE [-o OUT.ll] [--entry NAME]             compile to LLVM IR
  tomato build FILE [-o OUT] [--entry NAME]                  compile to IR, then link a native program with clang
  (compile and build also take --mode debug|normal|release; tomato explain CODE FILE decodes a normal-mode code)
  tomato bundle FILE [-o OUT] [--llvm FILE.ll ...]           one executable holding the program and the interpreter
"""
import os
import sys
import threading

from .bundle import compile_program
from .codegen import compile_to_ir
from .errors import TomatoError
from .interp import run_source

ENTRY_FLAG, MODE_FLAG = None, "debug"

USAGE = """usage: tomato run FILE [ENTRY [INPUTS...]] [--llvm FILE.ll ...]
       tomato compile FILE [-o OUT.ll] [--entry NAME] [--mode debug|normal|release]
       tomato build FILE [-o OUT] [--entry NAME] [--mode debug|normal|release] [--llvm FILE.ll ...]
       tomato explain CODE FILE
       tomato bundle FILE [-o OUT] [--llvm FILE.ll ...]

  FILE     the Tomato program
  ENTRY    the entry point to run, written without the @ (default: main)
  INPUTS   values for the entry point's parameters, in order
  --llvm   LLVM IR that `!name(...)` calls can use when running (needs llvmlite)
  compile  checks FILE and writes LLVM IR (default OUT: FILE with .ll). LLVM's tools turn that into any target.
           Only a core subset compiles so far; the rest stops with "the compiler does not support ... yet".
  build    compile, then link a native program with clang and the C runtime (and any --llvm IR files, which
           define the `!name` functions the program declares); run it as: ./OUT [INPUTS...]
  explain  turns an error code printed by a normal-mode program, such as E03:12, into the full message and the
           source line it came from; give it the same FILE the program was built from
  --mode   how a compiled program reports errors: debug (full messages, the default), normal (short codes
           for `explain`) or release (nothing readable)
  bundle   checks FILE and writes one executable that holds the program and the Python interpreter (not native);
           run it as: ./OUT [ENTRY [INPUTS...]]"""



def read_args(argv):
    """Split argv into positional words, --llvm IR files, -o OUT and --entry NAME."""
    args, llvm_ir, out, k = [], [], None, 1
    global ENTRY_FLAG, MODE_FLAG
    ENTRY_FLAG, MODE_FLAG = None, "debug"
    while k < len(argv):
        if argv[k] == "--llvm" and k + 1 < len(argv):
            with open(argv[k + 1], encoding="utf-8") as f:
                llvm_ir.append((argv[k + 1], f.read()))
            k += 2
        elif argv[k] == "-o" and k + 1 < len(argv):
            out = argv[k + 1]
            k += 2
        elif argv[k] == "--entry" and k + 1 < len(argv):
            ENTRY_FLAG = argv[k + 1]
            k += 2
        elif argv[k] == "--mode" and k + 1 < len(argv):
            MODE_FLAG = argv[k + 1]
            k += 2
        else:
            args.append(argv[k])
            k += 1
    return args, llvm_ir, out


def main(argv):
    try:
        args, llvm_ir, out = read_args(argv)
    except OSError as err:
        print("error: cannot read %s: %s" % (err.filename, err.strerror), file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    cmd = args[0] if args else None
    if cmd == "explain":
        return explain_code(args[1:])
    if len(args) < 2 or cmd not in ("run", "compile", "build", "bundle") or (cmd != "run" and len(args) != 2) \
            or (cmd == "run" and (out or ENTRY_FLAG)) or (cmd == "compile" and llvm_ir):
        print(USAGE, file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    path = args[1]
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            src = f.read()
    except OSError as err:
        print("error: cannot read %s: %s" % (path, err.strerror), file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    search = [os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path))]
    base = path[:-4] if path.endswith(".tom") else path
    try:
        if cmd == "bundle":
            target = out or base
            mods = compile_program(src, target, search=search, llvm_ir=llvm_ir)
            print("wrote %s%s" % (target, " (bundles modules: %s)" % ", ".join(mods) if mods else ""))
        elif cmd == "compile":
            target = out or base + ".ll"
            with open(target, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                f.write(compile_to_ir(src, ENTRY_FLAG or "main", search, MODE_FLAG))
            print("wrote %s" % target)
        elif cmd == "build":
            return build_native(src, out or base, ENTRY_FLAG or "main", search, MODE_FLAG, llvm_ir)
        else:
            entry, inputs = (args[2] if len(args) > 2 else "main"), args[3:]
            run_source(src, entry=entry, llvm_ir=llvm_ir, inputs=inputs, search=search)
    except TomatoError as e:
        print("error: %s" % e, file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    return 0


def explain_code(args):
    from .errcodes import explain
    if len(args) != 2:
        print(USAGE, file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    try:
        with open(args[1], encoding="utf-8") as f:
            print(explain(args[0], f.read()))
    except OSError as err:
        print("error: cannot read %s: %s" % (args[1], err.strerror), file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    except ValueError as err:
        print("error: %s" % err, file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    return 0


def build_native(src, target, entry, search, mode="debug", extra_ir=()):
    """Compile to IR in a temporary folder and link it with the C runtime using clang."""
    import shutil
    import subprocess
    import tempfile
    clang = shutil.which("clang")
    if not clang:
        print("error: tomato build needs clang on the PATH", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    ir = compile_to_ir(src, entry, search, mode)
    runtime = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "runtime", "tomato_rt.c")
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        ll = os.path.join(d, "program.ll")
        with open(ll, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(ir)
        inputs = [ll]
        for k, (label, text) in enumerate(extra_ir):     # LLVM IR given with --llvm is linked in (D27)
            path = os.path.join(d, "extra%d.ll" % k)
            with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                f.write(text)
            inputs.append(path)
        r = subprocess.run([clang, "-O1", "-Wno-override-module", "-x", "ir"] + inputs + ["-x", "c", runtime, "-lm",
                            "-o", target], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        print("error: clang failed:\n%s" % r.stderr.strip(), file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print("wrote %s" % target)
    return 0


def run_bundle(data, argv):
    """Entry point of a file written by `tomato compile`: ./OUT [ENTRY [INPUTS...]]."""
    sys.setrecursionlimit(500000)
    threading.stack_size(512 * 1024 * 1024)
    result = []

    def go():
        entry, inputs = (argv[1] if len(argv) > 1 else "main"), argv[2:]
        try:
            run_source(data["program"], entry=entry, modules=data["modules"], inputs=inputs,
                       llvm_ir=[tuple(x) for x in data["llvm_ir"]] or None)
            result.append(0)
        except TomatoError as e:
            print("error: %s" % e, file=sys.stderr)
            result.append(1)

    t = threading.Thread(target=go)
    t.start()
    t.join()
    return result[0] if result else 1


def main_big_stack(argv):
    """Run on a thread with a large stack so deep Tomato recursion does not overflow the host."""
    sys.setrecursionlimit(500000)
    threading.stack_size(512 * 1024 * 1024)
    result = []
    t = threading.Thread(target=lambda: result.append(main(argv)))
    t.start()
    t.join()
    return result[0] if result else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main_big_stack(sys.argv))
files.tomato/bundle.py:
"""`tomato compile`: write one standalone executable file for a Tomato program.

PROVISIONAL (P35): the file is a Python zip application holding the checked program, every module it imports, any
LLVM IR given with --llvm, and the interpreter. It is not native code yet; native LLVM compilation is the later
Tomato-in-Tomato compiler. Run the result as `./OUT [ENTRY [INPUTS...]]`.
"""
import io
import json
import os
import stat
import sys
import zipfile

from .errors import TomatoError
from .interp import Interpreter

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
RUNNER = '''import sys
sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[0])
import _program
from tomato.__main__ import run_bundle
sys.exit(run_bundle(_program.DATA, sys.argv))
'''


def compile_program(src, out_path, search=None, llvm_ir=None):
    """Check `src` and write the executable; returns the names of the modules bundled."""
    interp = Interpreter(search=search, llvm_ir=None)   # IR is only bundled here, not run
    interp.check(src)
    modules = {k: v for k, v in interp.module_text.items() if k != "builtin" and not _is_std(k)}
    data = {"program": src, "modules": modules, "llvm_ir": [[a, b] for a, b in (llvm_ir or [])]}
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    with zipfile.ZipFile(buf, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as z:
        z.writestr("__main__.py", RUNNER)
        z.writestr("_program.py", "import json\nDATA = json.loads(%s)\n" % repr(json.dumps(data)))
        for root, _, files in os.walk(HERE):
            for f in sorted(files):
                if f.endswith((".py", ".tom")):
                    full = os.path.join(root, f)
                    z.write(full, os.path.join("tomato", os.path.relpath(full, HERE)))
    # A shell prefix, not a #! line, because the interpreter's path may contain spaces. Programs that call LLVM
    # need the Python that has llvmlite; others use whatever python3 is on the PATH.
    py = sys.executable if llvm_ir else "python3"
    prefix = "#!/bin/sh\nexec '%s' \"$0\" \"$@\"\n" % py.replace("'", "'\\''")
    with open(out_path, "wb") as f:
        f.write(prefix.encode() + buf.getvalue())
    os.chmod(out_path, os.stat(out_path).st_mode | stat.S_IXUSR | stat.S_IXGRP | stat.S_IXOTH)
    return sorted(modules)


def _is_std(name):
    return os.path.isfile(os.path.join(HERE, "std", name + ".tom"))
files.tomato/errcodes.py:
"""Error codes for compiled programs (D34a, P37).

Normal mode prints `error CODE` where CODE is `E<kind>:<line>`, for example `E03:12`. `tomato explain CODE FILE`
decodes it against the source file into the full debug-style message. Release mode prints nothing.
The numbers are PROVISIONAL and may change until Davis decides the format.
"""
import re

KINDS = {
    1: ("overflow", "integer overflow: the result does not fit the integer type (D05e, D05n)"),
    2: ("division by zero", "division by zero (D05ab)"),
    3: ("modulo by zero", "modulo by zero (D05au)"),
    4: ("range step", "range step cannot be zero"),
    5: ("conversion", "integer conversion out of range for the destination type (D05p)"),
    6: ("missing return", "the function ended without returning a value"),
    7: ("index", "index out of range (D20a, D17c)"),
    8: ("class conversion", "the object is not an instance of that class (D12az, D12bh)"),
    9: ("duplicate key", "duplicate key in a dict literal"),
    10: ("key not found", "the key or element is not there (D20b)"),
    11: ("uncaught", "an error was raised and never caught (D22a)"),
    12: ("none", "None where a value is needed (D23b)"),
}
BY_NAME = {name: code for code, (name, _) in KINDS.items()}
CODE = re.compile(r"^E(\d{2}):(\d+)$")


def code_for(kind):
    return BY_NAME[kind]


def explain(code, source):
    """Return the full readable text for CODE given the program's source text; raises ValueError for a bad code."""
    m = CODE.match(code.strip())
    if not m or int(m.group(1)) not in KINDS:
        raise ValueError("not a Tomato error code: %r (codes look like E03:12)" % code)
    kind, line = int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2))
    lines = source.split("\n")
    out = ["error %s: %s" % (code.strip(), KINDS[kind][1])]
    if 1 <= line <= len(lines):
        text = lines[line - 1]
        out.append("  --> line %d" % line)
        out.append("   %d | %s" % (line, text))
        out.append("   %s | %s^" % (" " * len(str(line)), " " * (len(text) - len(text.lstrip()))))
    else:
        raise ValueError("line %d is not in this file (it has %d lines): is this the program the code came from?"
                         % (line, len(lines)))
    return "\n".join(out)
files.tomato/nodes.py:
class Node:
    _fields = ()

    def __init__(self, *args, line=None):
        for f, a in zip(self._fields, args):
            setattr(self, f, a)
        self.line = line

    def __repr__(self):
        return "%s(%s)" % (type(self).__name__, ", ".join(repr(getattr(self, f)) for f in self._fields))


def node(name, *fields):
    return type(name, (Node,), {"_fields": fields})


# type references and expressions
TypeRef = node("TypeRef", "name", "length", "arg", "arg2")   # length: expr or None; arg/arg2: type arguments of list, set, map
IntLit = node("IntLit", "value")
StrLit = node("StrLit", "value")
ListLit = node("ListLit", "items")
MapLit = node("MapLit", "pairs")                     # [(key, value)]
SetLit = node("SetLit", "items")
BoolLit = node("BoolLit", "value")
Name = node("Name", "name")
LlvmRef = node("LlvmRef", "name")
Attr = node("Attr", "obj", "name")
Call = node("Call", "func", "args")
TypeCall = node("TypeCall", "type", "args")          # int[length=8](x)
Index = node("Index", "obj", "index")
Slice = node("Slice", "obj", "lo", "hi")
BinOp = node("BinOp", "op", "left", "right")
UnOp = node("UnOp", "op", "operand")
# statements
Assign = node("Assign", "target", "value")
Declare = node("Declare", "name", "type", "value")
Return = node("Return", "value")
If = node("If", "branches", "orelse")                # branches: [(cond, body)]
While = node("While", "cond", "body")
For = node("For", "var", "iter", "body")
ExprStmt = node("ExprStmt", "expr")
Pass = node("Pass")
Break = node("Break")
Continue = node("Continue")
Raise = node("Raise", "value")
Try = node("Try", "body", "handlers", "orelse", "final")   # handlers: [(class name, var or None, body)]
Import = node("Import", "module", "names")
# declarations
Param = node("Param", "name", "type", "default")
FuncDef = node("FuncDef", "name", "params", "ret", "body", "private", "override", "marker")
FieldDef = node("FieldDef", "name", "type", "private", "const", "value")
ClassDef = node("ClassDef", "name", "parent", "interfaces", "fields", "methods")
InterfaceDef = node("InterfaceDef", "name", "parents", "methods")
Implements = node("Implements", "cls", "iface")
LlvmDecl = node("LlvmDecl", "name", "params", "ret")
Module = node("Module", "body")
